newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer walks away from New York soap opera trial. [CORRECTED 02:18 GMT 01/05]
newsitem.headline: Lawyer walks away from New York soap opera trial. [CORRECTED 02:18 GMT 01/05]

text.p: Disbarred personal injury attorney Burton Pugach received what amounted to a proverbial slap on the wrist from a jury Wednesday when he was convicted of one minor count of second degree harassment against a former mistress.
Pugach, the notorious lawyer who decades ago committed one of New York City's most sensational crimes of passion, could be sentenced May 8 to a maximum of just 15 days in jail.
Pugach, 70, came out of the courtroom raging. He said the jury used their "common sense" in reaching a verdict and he would sue his former mistress because she "framed me."
During the two week trial, Pugach acted as his own attorney, cross-examined the former mistress about their affair and called his wife as a character witness.

His wife is 60-year-old Linda Riss, a woman he had thugs attack with lye in 1959 when she tried to end their affair after finding out he was married. The 1959 attack left her disfigured and blind and he spent 14 years in prison for the crime. After his release, he divorced his wife and married Riss.

Riss, who stood by Pugach throughout the bizarre trial, described him as a "wonderful, caring husband" and testified that Pugach began the affair after she had heart surgery in 1990 and could not have sex with her husband. Riss said after the verdict: "The lesson here is 'no more ladies.'"
Pugach was found guilty by a Queens Criminal Court jury of only one minor violation out of 12 charges brought against him by the former mistress.

He was acquitted of aggravated harassment, menacing, sexual abuse and criminal contempt. The 42-year-old woman claimed he threatened to kill her after she tried to break off their 5-year relationship last fall.

The woman testified that Pugach told her that if she had dinner and sex with him, he would cancel the order to kill her. "'I won't blind you like I did with Linda because you have a big mouth,'" she quoted Pugach as telling her.

Testimony in the trial ended Friday when Pugach took the witness stand and swore to the jury that he was "an honourable man." In a 45-minute impassioned monologue that he said was "more like a soap opera," Pugach recounted intimate details of his extramarital affair and vehemently denied the charges.
